newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end higher on ADM, crush ideas.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end higher on ADM, crush ideas.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended higher on Wednesday on news an ADM crusher would be shut for the rest of the crop year which fueled ideas crushing levels would drop, traders said.

"The meal was up on expectations that there will be a reduced crush pace," said Bob Lekberg, analyst with Goldenberg-Hehmeyer. "We've been at a record crush pace and the feeling is that's going to turn down."
ADM on Wednesday announced it will close its Clarksdale, Mississippi crushing plant for the rest of the crop year. Three other plants will run on reduced rates, ADM said.
"The fact that ADM did announce it was cutting back was supportive to meal because the meal demand is still out there," said Joe Victor, analyst at Allendale Inc.
Soymeal was also boosted by rumors China had purchased South American soymeal. Argentine sources could not confirm the rumors.
Commercials were buyers of soymeal and soyoil on the day, contributing to talk of export demand and slowed crush rates.
Soymeal ended $4.70 to $0.80 per ton higher with May up $4.70 at $274.20. Soyoil closed 0.03 to 0.15 cent per lb higher with May up 0.06 at 24.69.
The March soymeal contract expired $2.90 per ton higher at $275.70 on Wednesday, pulling nearby contracts up with it.
"March meal went off very strong with no deliveries posted," a trader said. "As soon as it went off the board, funds started buying (deferreds)."
Traders said cash meal was at a premium to futures. Firms were reluctant to deliver against futures positions when they could get a better price in the cash market, traders said.
On the day, Cargill Inc bought 800 lots May, 500 July and 100 August soymeal. Continental Grain bought 400 May and ABN-AMRO Chicago Corp bought 200 July and 100 May.
In soyoil, Cargill bought 900 May and 100 July and ADM bought 300 May. Prudential Securities sold 400 May and Dean Witter sold 200 May and 200 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 18,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 27,188 lots. Soyoil volume was estimated at 12,000 lots, against Tuesday's actual volume of 19,120 lots.
